title: Salary to Hourly Calculator
subtitle: Convert annual salary to hourly wage — or hourly rate to yearly income. Includes all pay frequencies.
ptoHint: If you get paid vacation, enter the number of weeks. These weeks still count as paid hours.
resultDisclaimer: Gross pay only — does not include taxes, deductions, or overtime. For take-home estimates, use a paycheck calculator with your state and filing status.
commonText: The table below shows the annual, monthly, and weekly equivalents for common hourly rates, assuming 40 hours per week and 52 weeks per year (2,080 hours).
formula1: Annual salary → hourly rate: Annual ÷ (Hours per week × Weeks per year)
formula2: Hourly rate → annual salary: Hourly × Hours per week × Weeks per year
formula3: Weekly pay: Hourly × Hours per week
formulaNote: Standard full-time work assumes 2,080 hours per year (40 hours × 52 weeks). If you get paid time off, your effective working weeks are lower but your annual salary stays the same — the calculator handles this when you enter PTO weeks.
howTo1: Choose your direction: Salary → Hourly, or Hourly → Salary.
howTo2: Enter your annual salary or hourly rate.
howTo3: Adjust hours per week (default 40) and weeks per year (default 52).
howTo4: If you receive paid vacation, expand Advanced options and enter PTO weeks.
howTo5: Click "Calculate" to see the full breakdown across all pay frequencies.
faq1q: $25 an hour is how much a year?
faq1a: At 40 hours per week and 52 weeks per year, $25/hour equals $52,000 per year, or $4,333 per month and $1,000 per week.
faq2q: $50,000 a year is how much an hour?
faq2a: A $50,000 annual salary works out to $24.04 per hour at 40 hours per week and 52 weeks per year.
faq3q: What is the difference between salary and hourly?
faq3a: Salaried employees receive a fixed annual amount regardless of hours worked, and often receive benefits like paid time off and health insurance. Hourly employees are paid per hour worked, may receive overtime (1.5× rate above 40 hours/week in the US), but typically have less predictable income.
faq4q: How many hours are in a work year?
faq4a: A standard full-time work year is 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks). Some employers calculate based on 2,000 hours (50 weeks) to account for two weeks of unpaid time off.
faq5a: No. This calculator shows gross pay only. Your actual take-home pay will be lower after federal income tax, state tax, Social Security, and Medicare. Use a paycheck calculator for your state to estimate net pay.
faq6q: How do I calculate my hourly rate for a freelance project?
faq6a: Freelancers should target an hourly rate that covers not just working hours, but also admin time, taxes, insurance, and unpaid time off. A common rule of thumb: aim for 2-3× the hourly rate of a comparable salaried position.
disclaimer: Disclaimer: This calculator provides estimates for informational purposes. Actual pay may vary based on overtime, bonuses, benefits, and employer-specific policies. Always verify with your employer or payroll provider.
footer: Runs entirely in your browser. No data is collected or stored.
